section_summary: This section covers diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence from January 1940 to May 1941 regarding requested visits by Japanese naval transports and training vessels to ports in the Philippine Islands, primarily Manila and Davao. The Japanese Embassy submitted formal notifications and requests for courtesies, provisions, and crew shore leave for the transports Shiriya, Hayatomo, and Iro, the naval training ships Katori and Kashima, and the merchant marine training vessel Kaio Maru. The Department of State routinely coordinated these requests with the War Department, Navy Department, Department of the Interior, and the United States High Commissioner in Manila, granting clearances before several visits were subsequently rescheduled or canceled by the Japanese government. Cross-reference notes also record inquiries regarding Japanese vessel movements to Hawaii and the application of U.S. alien seamen visa regulations.
